contexts.description: Provides reusable 3D and motion-rich UI primitives used across landing and feature surfaces: a tilt-reactive Card3D with spring physics and glare overlay, a ParallaxSection for depth-layered scroll, FloatingElements for ambient decorative animation, and an InteractivePreview modal. All components share a ReducedMotionProvider that reads the OS `prefers-reduced-motion` media query and exposes tiered motion capabilities (full → reduced → minimal) so every animation degrades gracefully for accessibility.
contexts.name: 3d-visual-effects

contexts.description: Achievement and award system that recognises user milestones. Achievement cards can be revealed, shared via a share modal, and embedded as standalone pages with OG meta tags. The Awards feature displays a leaderboard-style award list with lazy loading. API routes handle achievement OG-image rendering and share-code generation.
contexts.name: achievements-awards

contexts.description: AI agent integration and user-personalization subsystem. agent-bridge exposes a secure channel for Claude/AI agents to read and write task memory within the app. PersonalizationEngine tracks user interests and runs A/B tests to select showcased content. GlobalOrchestrator routes user commands across feature stores; lazy-store-accessor provides deferred Zustand access to avoid circular imports.
contexts.name: agent-and-personalization

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/v1/analytics, GET /api/v1/trends, GET /api/personalization/recommend, POST /api/personalization/track, GET /api/recommendation, GET /api/activities, POST /api/embed/analytics
contexts.description: Creator analytics dashboard and the personalisation/recommendation engine. The dashboard shows list performance sparklines and analytics cards for list creators. API routes cover activity feeds, trend data, category browsing, personalised profile/track/recommend endpoints, the public v1 analytics and SDK endpoints, and embedded/share analytics ingestion.
contexts.name: analytics-personalization

contexts.description: Design-system foundation for motion, timing, and visual tokens. motion-tokens defines the base easing and duration scale; motion-presets packages them into named variants (page-enter, card-hover, etc.); micro-interactions and scroll-triggers add contextual animation behaviors; badge-tokens and timing constants ensure cross-component consistency.
contexts.name: animations-and-tokens

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/lists, GET /api/top/groups, GET /api/criteria, POST /api/lists, Supabase RPC
contexts.description: Central HTTP and database client layer for all server-side data access. Includes a typed ApiClient with circuit breaker and rate limiter, Supabase client/server helpers, Gemini AI provider, and TanStack Query key factories that keep cache invalidation consistent across the app. Covers list, collection, criteria, top-items, wiki-images, and public-API endpoints.
contexts.name: api-client-layer

contexts.description: Provides the global application frame: root layout, CSS tokens, global error boundaries, offline fallback, and auth callback. Also contains the CommandPalette feature which gives users a keyboard-driven interface to navigate lists and actions. These files form the outermost layer every page shares.
contexts.name: app-shell

contexts.description: Provides the user-facing authentication layer (sign-in modal, user menu, auth prompts, toast notifications) alongside app-level shell components: animated CTA buttons, a session progress indicator, an integrated audio/YouTube player for media-backed lists, a quick-share menu, and a dev-only prefetch analytics panel.
contexts.name: app-shell-auth

contexts.description: Manages the user's item backlog (the pool of candidates not yet placed on the grid) and user-created list collections. The backlog store is modularized into action slices (data loading, group management, item CRUD, offline sync, utilities) backed by an IndexedDB persistent cache; a fast item index enables O(1) lookups. The collection-store tracks ListCollection metadata and hierarchical tree nodes used to organise multiple ranked lists.
contexts.name: backlog-catalog-state

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/blueprints, GET/PUT/DELETE /api/blueprints/[slugOrId], POST /api/blueprints/[slugOrId]/clone, POST /api/blueprints/[slugOrId]/rate, POST /api/studio/generate, GET /api/generate-ai-image
contexts.description: Blueprint and template system: community-published list blueprints that users can clone, rate, and view, plus the community template gallery card component. API routes handle blueprint CRUD, publishing, cloning, and view/rate actions. The studio sub-routes support AI image search, YouTube lookup, and item matching to power the studio editor.
contexts.name: blueprints-templates

contexts.description: Cross-cutting persistence layer covering server-side caching, unified client-side cache, IndexedDB/localStorage adapters, and offline-first sync. UnifiedCache wraps both server and client caches; OfflineProvider detects network loss; useOfflineSync queues mutations and replays them on reconnect; UnsavedChangesBanner warns users of pending local writes.
contexts.name: cache-and-storage

contexts.description: Powers gamification and social engagement: ChallengeManager handles time-boxed ranking challenges; ShareChainTracker follows viral sharing chains; StreakTracker rewards daily ranking activity; InvitationSystem manages friend invites; CollaborativeRanking enables real-time co-ranking; debate-provider structures async item debates; EmbedCodeGenerator lets users embed their ranked lists on external sites.
contexts.name: challenges-and-engagement

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/challenges, POST /api/challenges/join, GET /api/challenges/[id]/leaderboard, POST /api/challenges/[id]/submit, GET/POST /api/share, GET /api/share/[code], POST /api/share/[code]/fork
contexts.description: Competitive challenges and result-sharing features. API routes handle challenge CRUD, joining, streak tracking, chain challenges, invitations, leaderboards, and submission. The share system lets users publish their completed ranking with a unique code, fork others' rankings, and view shared result pages. Bookmarks and debate votes are also managed here.
contexts.name: challenges-sharing

contexts.description: State management, hooks, and the collections dashboard for user-owned grouped lists. Covers filter state, visible-item pagination, intersection observer, quick-select, drag-reorder support, adaptive loading, and the Collections dashboard UI with a list manager, sidebar, and quick-switcher. Users manage their personal collections of ranked lists here.
contexts.name: collection-management

contexts.description: The visual components of the item collection panel used inside the ranking session: activity timeline, add-item modal, ranking distribution chart, mini trajectory chart, metadata grid, item inspector popup, criteria scoring section, and lazy-load trigger for infinite scrolling. These components surface per-item detail and ranking context to the user.
contexts.name: collection-panel-ui

contexts.description: Shared utility belt consumed by every other lib context: general-purpose helpers (getColors, getIcons, getCompletionStyles), category/match config, scoring constants, showcase examples, item transform/validation utilities, list templates, activity logging, and debug logger. These have no feature ownership — they are stable primitives that keep business modules thin.
contexts.name: core-utilities

contexts.description: Provides unified data access and authentication primitives for the entire application. Wraps Supabase client, TanStack Query, and auth state into composable hooks, handling optimistic updates, cache invalidation, session management, and guest-to-user identity merging on sign-in.
contexts.name: data-auth-hooks

contexts.description: Defines and seeds the core Supabase PostgreSQL schema for the GOAT application. Contains table definitions for items, item groups, lists, and list-item rankings, plus a migration adding list type/description, award category seed data, and JS/SQL scripts for populating and updating game image records.
contexts.name: database-schema-and-seeds

contexts.description: Developer tooling for recording implementation progress to a local SQLite log and for seeding the Supabase database with categorised item catalogs. The logging scripts write structured entries (requirement name, overview, tested flag) to an `implementation_log` table; the seeding script uses Gemini to generate item titles, resolves cover art via IGDB/Wikipedia, and bulk-upserts records into Supabase.
contexts.name: dev-logging-and-seeding

contexts.description: Implements the drag-and-drop protocol that lets users physically arrange items into ranked positions and tier rows. Routes drag events through typed operation classes (assign, move, swap, tier transfer, unrank) and validates each action before committing state. Depends on @dnd-kit and coordinates with grid-store and session-store via the unified transfer protocol.
contexts.name: drag-drop-engine

contexts.description: Provides attribute-based facet navigation on top of the filter system, letting users drill into item collections by categorical dimensions (genre, year, platform, etc.). FacetExtractor derives facet values from item data; FacetAggregator counts occurrences; FacetPanel and MobileFacetDrawer render the UI. The module exists both as a standalone lib and as a sub-module re-exported from filters.
contexts.name: faceted-search

contexts.description: TypeScript type definitions for the application's core feature domains: items, collections, ranking modes (podium, bracket, tier list), match sessions, backlog groups, consensus, sharing, studio, and YouTube integration. These types form the shared data contracts consumed by stores, API routes, and UI components across all features. Depends on placed-item and lib/tiers utilities.
contexts.name: feature-domain-types

contexts.description: Unified error handling and user-feedback pipeline. GoatError defines a typed error hierarchy; ErrorBoundary catches React render errors; api-error-handler normalizes API responses; error-analytics tracks error rates; ErrorNotificationToast surfaces them to users. The feedback-pipeline provides a modal flow with progress, particles, and state transitions for async operations like saving and sharing.
contexts.name: feedback-and-errors

contexts.description: Full-text and smart-query filtering of item collections, with real-time UI components for filter panels, presets, autocomplete, and sort selectors. FilterEngine evaluates filter predicates; SmartQueryParser interprets natural-language queries into structured filters. Integrates with collection state and TanStack Query for live counts.
contexts.name: filter-and-search

contexts.description: Generates shareable result cards and Open Graph images for ranked lists. LayoutEngine and BalanceOptimizer arrange item thumbnails; ColorAnalyzer picks a palette from cover art; ImageEnhancer post-processes the canvas; OGCardGenerator assembles the final card using card-layout templates (Grid, List, Featured). A per-session CacheManager avoids redundant renders.
contexts.name: image-and-og

contexts.description: Utilities for auditing and repairing item image URLs across the database. Scripts validate URL reachability (HTTP HEAD checks), detect images hosted on non-whitelisted domains, and replace broken URLs by querying Wikipedia or IGDB as fallbacks. They operate against the live Supabase API or directly against the database and support dry-run and filtered modes.
contexts.name: image-data-maintenance

contexts.description: Shared behavioural hooks for drag-and-drop physics (gravity wells, magnetic snap, velocity tracking) and list virtualization (lazy-load and intersection-observer), packaged as framework-agnostic utilities that feature code imports rather than reimplements. These patterns underpin the match grid's tactile feel and the backlog panel's scroll performance.
contexts.name: interaction-patterns

contexts.description: Renders backlog and grid items at varying fidelity levels — from the compact flip-card used inside the match grid to the full RichItemCard with gallery, metadata badges, quick-actions, and expanded preview. The two tiers (ui/item-card and RichItemCard) share a flip-reveal animation pattern and are consumed by both the collection panels and the grid.
contexts.name: item-display

contexts.api_surface: Consumes IGDB, TMDB, Spotify, Wikipedia, YouTube, Leonardo external APIs
contexts.description: Fetches metadata and images for rankable items from external providers (IGDB, Spotify, TMDB, Wikipedia, Leonardo AI, YouTube). EnrichmentPipeline orchestrates multi-source lookups; SourceRouter picks the right fetcher per category; DataNormalizer aligns heterogeneous payloads into a common item shape. Latency per source is tracked to inform future routing decisions.
contexts.name: item-enrichment

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/top/groups, GET /api/top/groups/[id]/items, GET/POST /api/items, GET /api/items/[id]/details, POST /api/items/batch-enrich, GET /api/search
contexts.description: API routes for the item and category catalog: top-group management (bulk load, category browse, search suggestions), individual item CRUD with enrichment, stats, and validation, plus collection CRUD and global search. These routes feed the backlog panels and item pickers throughout the app.
contexts.name: items-catalog-api

contexts.description: The main home page and list-creation entry point. Renders the onboarding hero, showcase cards, neon-arena theming, and the composition modal users open to create a new ranked list from a template. Depends on TanStack Query for list data and Framer Motion for animations.
contexts.name: landing-home

contexts.description: Flexible panel-and-window layout primitives used throughout the match and collection interfaces. LayoutManager coordinates responsive breakpoints; ContainerProvider injects dimensions into children; DetachableWindow and PictureInPicture let users pop panels out; ResizableHandle and CollapsiblePanel give manual control over panel sizing. All components respect touch gestures via TouchGestureHandler.
contexts.name: layout-system

contexts.description: The browsable list sections shown on the home page: featured lists, saved lists, user-owned lists, bookmarked items, a search/filter bar, and a resume-ranking progress bar. Each section fetches its own slice of data and renders preview cards with popover thumbnails, giving users a way to find and resume ranking sessions.
contexts.name: list-discovery

contexts.description: Manages CRUD operations, navigation, and analytics for ranked lists and their item collections. Covers list creation from blueprints, thumbnail generation, preview prefetching, bookmark/collection management, and progress tracking through the ranking session lifecycle.
contexts.name: list-ranking-hooks

contexts.description: Handles the multi-step composition modal where users configure a new ranked list — choosing category, list size, time period, and preview. It embeds a hierarchical CategoryBrowser with breadcrumb navigation and search, and a SizeVisualizer that animates grid previews and estimates completion time, giving users a concrete sense of scope before starting a match session.
contexts.name: list-setup-modal

contexts.description: API routes for list lifecycle and ranking data: creating, reading, and updating lists with their items, criteria, and thumbnails; the public v1 rankings endpoints for submitting and aggregating community rank scores; consensus submission; and the ranking-graph history endpoints. This is the core data layer for the ranked-list domain.
contexts.name: lists-rankings-api

contexts.description: Tournament-style bracket ranking mode as an alternative to drag-and-drop. Users pick winners in head-to-head matchups; a seeding engine generates the bracket and a visualization renders the bracket tree. Upon completion a standings/stats/trophy tab set summarises results.
contexts.name: match-bracket

contexts.description: The sidebar / horizontal-bar backlog panel from which users drag items onto the ranking grid. Supports virtualized grid layout, mobile swipeable items, search/filter within the panel, and a resizable panel handle. This is the source side of the drag-and-drop pipeline.
contexts.name: match-collections-panel

contexts.description: Powers the core match session experience: item comparison selection, drag-and-drop synchronization, criteria-based scoring, consensus calculation, and debate-style head-to-head flows. Bridges the Zustand comparison/criteria stores with TanStack Query for database persistence.
contexts.name: match-comparison-hooks

contexts.description: Top-level Match feature UI: the goat and award route pages, the comparison modal, and all mid-level match components including list-settings, criteria scoring, position change indicators, AI suggestion overlay, sync status, and mobile long-press preview. This is the orchestration layer users interact with when actively ranking items.
contexts.name: match-core-components

contexts.description: Grid drop-zone rendering and item badge overlays. Drop zones display celebration particles on successful drops, magnetic glow aura effects, and handle occupied/empty slot states. Item badges show average rank, consensus overlays, quick-select indicators, rank badges, and tier indicators so users can see community data while ranking.
contexts.name: match-drop-zone

contexts.description: The visual grid slot components: all view modes (Tier List, Podium, Mount Rushmore, GOAT), drag overlay, physics slots, swap animation, tier row/section rendering, screen-reader announcer, and the view-switcher. These components render the ranked positions and handle the target side of drag-and-drop interactions.
contexts.name: match-grid-slot-ui

contexts.description: The engine layer beneath the grid UI: physics simulation, smart layout, snap-to-grid, auto-arrange, haptic feedback, tier configuration data, and tier keyboard navigation/layout hooks. Also contains the debate/controversy panel that surfaces conflicting community rankings on grid items.
contexts.name: match-grid-system

contexts.description: Provides the in-session comparison and completion modals used during a match run. The comparison modal lets users side-by-side evaluate two items and choose between them, while the completion modal celebrates a finished ranking and surfaces share actions. Both modals read from and write to the match and comparison Zustand stores.
contexts.name: match-interaction-modals

contexts.description: Hooks, library utilities, and the share modal for the match feature. Covers AI image generation style presets, physics configuration, tier list export, medal styling, prompt building for result images, and touch/swipe/pinch-zoom gesture hooks. The ShareModal lets users share their completed ranked list.
contexts.name: match-logic

contexts.description: Owns all Zustand state for the core match-and-rank interaction loop: grid positions, drag-and-drop resolution, session persistence, item comparison, keyboard navigation, smart-fill placement, and undo history. The match-store orchestrates the other stores in this context, calling grid-store for position changes, session-store for persistence, comparison-store for side-by-side modal state, and placement-store for smart-fill. The item-store subdirectory holds pure utilities (normalized data shape, session lifecycle helpers, grid operation primitives) that session-store and grid-store import.
contexts.name: match-session-state

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/health, POST /api/sync, GET/POST /api/agent-bridge/tasks, POST /api/auth/merge-guest, GET /api/og/[listId], GET /api/oembed, POST /api/match/generate-result-image, GET /api/v1/widgets/embed.js
contexts.description: Cross-cutting platform API routes that do not belong to a single business feature: health checks, data sync, the agent-bridge task queue for AI assistant integration, guest-account merge on sign-in, batch processing, admin image search, OG/oEmbed image generation for social sharing, the embeddable widget JS, and the match result image generator.
contexts.name: platform-infrastructure

contexts.description: TypeScript type definitions for platform-level concerns: users, user preferences, API keys, API response envelopes, database schema types, AI image generation, composition-to-API mapping, and modal prop contracts. These types underpin authentication, data access, and cross-cutting UI patterns rather than any single feature domain.
contexts.name: platform-types

contexts.description: Bootstraps the React context tree with all global and route-scoped providers. QueryProvider initialises TanStack Query with a centralised cache config; BacklogProvider manages offline detection, periodic persistence and backend sync for backlog data; MatchProviders composes match-route-specific providers (BacklogProvider, OfflineProvider, ItemDetailPopupProvider) with idle-callback deferred mounting; DeferredProviders lazily mounts CommandPalette and PrefetchProvider after first paint to reduce critical-path JS; PrefetchProvider wires the PredictionEngine/RoutePreloader/PrefetchManager to the router. All five providers sit at the top of the provider hierarchy defined in src/app/layout.tsx and the (match) route group.
contexts.name: provider-composition

contexts.description: Provides the analytical layer on top of ranked data: a RankingEngine that scores items, a cross-list graph that surfaces universal ratings, criteria-based weighted scoring, and consensus analysis that detects controversy and trends across multiple users' rankings. ConsensusOverlay renders a heatmap of community agreement. Feeds the social features and result-image generation.
contexts.name: ranking-analytics

contexts.description: Aggregates the remaining Zustand stores that power ranking analysis and auxiliary UI features. ranking-store is the unified source of truth for tier lists, bracket state, and podium rankings across all display modes; ranking-graph-store tracks graph-based ranking visualisation; use-list-store holds current list metadata. Debate, consensus, and criteria stores support AI-assisted placement discussion and scoring rubrics. studio-store drives the AI list-creation wizard. layout-, audio-, wiki-image-, item-popup-, composition-modal-, drop-zone-highlight-, and registry stores cover responsive layout, sound feedback, image look-up, and shared UI overlay state.
contexts.name: ranking-ui-feature-state

contexts.description: Renders scored rankings as visual overlays and themed displays, adapting presentation to the content category (movies, music, sports, games). Score overlays (bar, ring, label) sit atop item images, while ThemedScoreDisplay and its category-specific renderers deliver richer contextual visualisations with animated progress bars.
contexts.name: score-display

contexts.description: Manages multi-platform sharing of ranked lists and result images, with platform-specific adapters for Twitter, Discord, Instagram, Reddit, WhatsApp, Telegram, LinkedIn, Facebook, email, native share, and clipboard copy. ShareManager orchestrates the flow; ContentOptimizer tailors copy per platform; DeepLinkGenerator builds trackable URLs; ShareAnalytics records share events.
contexts.name: sharing-platforms

contexts.description: Provides visual indicators for item position, tier membership, goal completion state, and progress rings — consumed across the grid and collection panels. GoalProgressRing and GoalCompletionBurst handle animated goal lifecycle feedback, while PositionBadge and TierIndicator mark rank context in list views.
contexts.name: status-badges

contexts.description: AI-assisted list creation studio where users describe a topic, let AI find and match items, then review and save their list. Provides a full editing UI: metadata panel, criteria editor, card preview, item cards grid, and a publish success flow. The studio page orchestrates the multi-step creation workflow.
contexts.name: studio-editor

contexts.description: Provides dark/light theme switching for the entire application via a thin wrapper around next-themes. Injects the ThemeProvider into the React tree (consumed by the root layout) so all components can read and toggle the active color scheme. The experimental-dark → dark CSS fallback is handled in globals.css rather than in JS, keeping this provider side-effect-free.
contexts.name: theme-provider

contexts.description: Manages the grid positions (1-50) and tier rows that hold ranked items, including boundary calculations, placement scoring, and inventory sorting. TierCalculator converts raw scores to tier labels; PlacementPredictor suggests the best drop zone for an incoming item. Consumed by the drag-drop engine and match feature components.
contexts.name: tier-grid-logic

contexts.description: Shared UI and interaction primitives used across all features: responsive breakpoints, motion preferences, swipe/tilt/animation hooks, prefetch strategies, toast notifications, undo keyboard shortcuts, search, and social sharing utilities. These have no business-domain knowledge and are pure UX infrastructure.
contexts.name: ui-interaction-hooks

contexts.description: The baseline component library for the application — buttons, modals, skeletons, grids, image handling, counters, and selection controls that every feature layer builds on. Stats-card, masonry-grid, and progressive-image handle data-dense layouts and performant media loading without feature-specific logic.
contexts.name: ui-primitives

contexts.description: Rendering-performance subsystem for large item collections: VirtualCollectionList virtualizes long lists; InfiniteLoader handles paginated fetching; ScrollPositionManager restores scroll on navigation; PrefetchManager predicts and prefetches routes using hover and scroll signals; GestureRecognizer detects swipes for mobile quick-rank interactions; PerfTimer instruments hot paths.
contexts.name: virtual-and-performance

contexts.description: Centralises decorative and illustrative elements — 3D floating objects with reduced-motion support, category-specific icon sets, particle and tag decorations for the landing showcase, empty-state and error illustrations, and the theme token index. These assets are consumed by feature surfaces for visual richness without owning any application state.
contexts.name: visual-assets

contexts.description: Provides the shared visual language for the application: a depth token system (elevation shadows, glow presets, surface colours), decoration components (Glow, Shimmer, GradientBorder), the branded GoatMascot SVG illustrations used for empty states, and RankingProgressLayer which injects reactive CSS custom properties as users fill ranking grid positions. Consumed across all feature areas that need consistent elevation, glow effects, or progress-driven ambient animation. Depends on the ranking-progress and motion-preference hooks.
contexts.name: visual-primitives
